content: Rifampin interacts with various drugs by altering their metabolism, primarily through its effects on hepatic and intestinal enzymes such as CYP3A4, CYP2C9, CYP2C19, CYP1A2, and transport proteins like P-glycoprotein (P-gp) and OATP. These interactions can either increase or decrease the levels and effects of the co-administered drugs, often necessitating dose adjustments, close monitoring, or the use of alternative therapies. Below are specific examples of these interactions: 1. Resmetirom: Rifampin increases the levels of resmetirom by inhibiting OATP1B1/3 transporters. Co-administration is not recommended. 2. Ribociclib: Rifampin decreases ribociclib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A inducers. 3. Rimegepant: Rifampin reduces rimegepant levels via CYP3A4 induction. Alternative drugs should be considered. 4. Ripretinib: Rifampin decreases ripretinib levels and its active metabolite (DP-5439) by inducing CYP3A4. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A inhibitors. 5. Ritonavir: Rifampin reduces ritonavir levels through CYP3A4 induction. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 6. Simvastatin: Rifampin decreases simvastatin levels by inducing CYP3A4. Alternative therapies are recommended. 7. Sofosbuvir/Velpatasvir: Rifampin reduces the efficacy of sofosbuvir and velpatasvir by inducing P-gp and CYP3A4. Co-administration is contraindicated. 8. Siponimod: Rifampin decreases siponimod levels via CYP3A4 and CYP2C9 metabolism. Avoid co-administration, especially in patients with specific CYP2C9 genotypes. 9. Tacrolimus: Rifampin reduces tacrolimus levels by inducing CYP3A4. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 10. Tizanidine: Rifampin decreases tizanidine levels via CYP1A2 induction. Co-administration is contraindicated. 11. Voriconazole: Rifampin significantly reduces voriconazole levels through CYP3A4 induction. Co-administration is contraindicated. 12. Venetoclax: Rifampin decreases venetoclax levels by inducing CYP3A4. Avoid co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A inducers. 13. Buprenorphine: Rifampin reduces buprenorphine levels (including buccal, subdermal, and transdermal forms) by inducing CYP3A4. Dose adjustments and close monitoring are required. 14. Bupropion: Rifampin decreases bupropion levels by inducing CYP2B6. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Cannabidiol: Rifampin reduces cannabidiol levels by inducing CYP3A4 and CYP2B6. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 16. Amitriptyline: Rifampin decreases amitriptyline levels via CYP3A4, CYP2C19, and P-gp induction. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Calcium Carbonate/Antacids: Rifampin absorption is reduced when co-administered with antacids. Administer rifampin at least one hour before antacids. 18. Atorvastatin: Rifampin decreases atorvastatin levels by inducing P-gp. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Belumosudil: Rifampin reduces belumosudil levels via CYP3A4 induction. Increase the belumosudil dose to 200 mg twice daily when co-administered. 20. Brivaracetam: Rifampin decreases brivaracetam levels by inducing CYP2C19. Double the brivaracetam dose during co-administration. 21. Brexpiprazole: Rifampin reduces brexpiprazole levels via CYP3A4 induction. Double the brexpiprazole dose over 1–2 weeks if co-administered. 22. Bosentan: Rifampin decreases bosentan levels by inducing CYP3A4 and CYP2C9. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Typhoid Vaccine (Live): Rifampin reduces the efficacy of the live typhoid vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 24. Zanubrutinib: Rifampin decreases zanubrutinib levels via CYP3A4 induction. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. 25. Abiraterone: Rifampin reduces abiraterone levels by inducing CYP3A4. If co-administration is unavoidable, increase the abiraterone dose frequency to twice daily. 26. Amikacin: Rifampin reduces amikacin levels via P-gp induction. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Amlodipine: Rifampin decreases amlodipine levels by inducing CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Artesunate: Rifampin reduces artesunate levels by inducing UGT metabolism. Monitor for decreased efficacy. 29. Azithromycin: Azithromycin increases rifampin levels via P-gp inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Bazedoxifene/Conjugated Estrogens: Rifampin reduces their levels via P-gp induction. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Bortezomib: Rifampin decreases bortezomib levels via CYP3A4 induction. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Cabazitaxel: Rifampin reduces cabazitaxel levels via CYP3A4 induction. Avoid co-administration. 33. Calcitriol: Rifampin decreases calcitriol levels by inducing CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Canagliflozin: Rifampin reduces canagliflozin levels by increasing metabolism. Use caution and consider alternative antihyperglycemic agents. 35. Tovofinib: Rifampin decreases tovofinib levels by inducing CYP2C8. Avoid co-administration with strong or moderate CYP2C8 inducers. These interactions highlight the importance of understanding rifampin's effects on drug metabolism and transport pathways.
